newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese bonds end higher after Buba deal.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese bonds end higher after Buba deal.

text.p: Portuguese bonds ended higher after a compromise between the Bundesbank and Bonn over a plan to revalue central bank gold reserves. Sentiment that the new French Socialist government could defend a weaker euro boosted prospects for the entry of "Club Med" countries to the euro, dealers said.
*Spread vs Spanish 10-yr cash -6 bps vs -9 bps cls

LISBON, June 3 (Reuter) - Portuguese bonds ended at the highs after the Bundesbank and Bonn reached a compromise over a plan to revalue central bank gold reserves, and dealers said they could rise further tomorrow.

Sentiment that the new French Socialist government could defend a weaker euro boosted prospects for the entry of "Club Med" countries to the euro and provided support to Portuguese bonds, dealers said.
"June futures are close to breaking strong resistance at 109.50," one futures dealer said. "If this very important level is broken, cash will take off tomorrow."

A fixed income analyst said: "The yield curve ended at the day's highs amid plenty of demand. Ten year bonds closed with a yield spread of 66 basis points against Bunds. The only reason why the spread did not drop below 65 bps was because of the 10-year Portuguese bond auction this morning."
